name: Catedral de Granada
description: The yellow cathedral that crowns Parque Central is Nicaragua's most famous postcard. Its neoclassical facade rose over the ruins of the churches the city lost in several fires.
tip: The best light for photos is between 8 and 10 in the morning

name: Parque Central
description: The social heart of the city. Vigorón sellers set up among the almond trees and benches. Vigorón is Granada's dish of yuca, chicharrón and cabbage salad.
tip: Try freshly made vigorón and pair it with a cold cacao drink

name: Calle La Calzada
description: Granada's liveliest pedestrian street: colonial houses turned into cafés, live music and street artists from afternoon until night.
tip: Walk it at dusk, when the lights come on and the musicians come out

name: Convento San Francisco
description: One of the oldest convents in Central America, now a museum. It holds the collection of pre-Columbian statues carved on Zapatera Island.
tip: The room with the Zapatera idols is the museum's must-see stop

name: Mercado Municipal
description: The market where the city gets its supplies: spices, seasonal fruit, ground cacao and the food stalls where Granada families eat everyday meals.
tip: Bring cash in small bills and go early

name: Muelle del Cocibolca
description: Where Granada meets the Great Lake. Boats leave the pier for Las Isletas, the archipelago formed by the eruption of the Mombacho volcano.
tip: The boat ride through Las Isletas takes an hour and is paid separately

name: Ferry crossing
description: The Lake Cocibolca crossing to the island. As you sail, the two volcanoes keep growing on the horizon until they fill the whole view.
tip: Ride on the upper deck to see the volcanoes head-on

name: Moyogalpa
description: The island's port of entry, at the foot of the Concepción volcano. Colorful streets, woodcraft workshops and the tour's first island café.
tip: You can rent motorbikes and bicycles here to explore the island

name: Ojo de Agua
description: A natural spring of water filtered through volcanic rock. Two pools of crystal-clear water surrounded by century-old trees and a vine for swinging into the water.
tip: Come wearing your swimsuit and bring a towel: the changing rooms are basic

name: Petroglifos de Altagracia
description: Stones engraved more than a thousand years ago by the peoples who lived on the island. Spirals, monkeys and human figures carved into volcanic rock.
tip: Ask the guide about the meaning of the double spirals

name: Playa Santo Domingo
address: Istmo de Istián, Isla de Ometepe
description: The volcanic-sand beach that connects the two volcanoes. The lake's waves make it feel like the open sea. It's the best place to watch the sunset.
tip: The wind blows hard in the afternoon: perfect for kitesurfing

name: Charco Verde
address: San José del Sur, Isla de Ometepe
description: A lagoon surrounded by dry forest, and a reserve for howler monkeys, herons and magpie-jays. Legend says Chico Largo, the owner of the lagoon, lives here.
tip: The full trail takes 40 minutes and there are almost always monkeys

name: Museo El Ceibo
address: San José del Sur, Isla de Ometepe
description: Two museums in one: the island's largest pre-Columbian archaeological collection and a museum of Nicaraguan currency from colonial times to today.
tip: Admission covers both museums, so don't stop at just one

name: Mirador del Maderas
description: A high point on the lower slope of the Maderas volcano, with views of the isthmus, Concepción and the whole lake. The cloud forest begins just above this viewpoint.
tip: The climb is dirt and rock: hiking shoes are a must

name: Catedral de León
description: The largest basilica in Central America and a World Heritage Site. Rubén Darío rests beneath its nave, guarded by a marble lion.
tip: Entry to the cathedral is free; going up to the rooftops is paid separately

name: White rooftops of the Cathedral
description: The whitewashed rooftop of the cathedral, with views of the Los Maribios volcanic chain: Momotombo, Telica and Cerro Negro in a single panorama.
tip: You climb barefoot and the white surface is dazzling: bring sunglasses

name: Museo Casa Rubén Darío
description: The house where the Prince of Castilian Letters grew up, with his manuscripts, his library and the poet's personal belongings.
tip: Ask them to read you the poem Darío wrote at thirteen

name: Historic center murals
description: A walking tour of the murals that tell the recent history of the university city, painted by student collectives and local artists.
tip: The biggest murals are on the main avenue

name: Mercado La Terminal
description: Here you taste the real food of León: nacatamal, quesillo with pickled onion and a tiste drink served in a gourd cup.
tip: The quesillo at the north corner is the locals' favorite

name: Finca Selva Negra
description: A mountain coffee farm founded by German settlers, now a model of sustainable production with protected cloud forest on its land.
tip: The mountain climate is cool: bring a light jacket

name: Wet mill
description: Where freshly picked coffee is pulped, fermented and washed. This step shapes much of the final flavor in the cup.
tip: Ask about the difference between the washed and honey processes

name: Drying patios
description: The patios and African beds where coffee dries in the sun for days, turned by hand several times a day so it loses moisture evenly.
tip: At midday you can watch the beans being turned

name: Roasting workshop
description: Here green beans become coffee. Roast profiles are explained, and each visitor roasts their own sample to take home.
tip: The coffee you roast goes home with you, packaged: it's part of the tour

name: Coffee tasting
description: A cupping table with five cups from different altitudes and processes. You learn the cupping protocol: aroma, breaking the crust, slurp and notes.
tip: Don't have a heavy breakfast beforehand: your palate works best when it's clean

name: Mountain viewpoint
description: A high point above the coffee plantations with views of the Matagalpa valley. With luck, you'll see quetzals and toucans in the shade forest.
tip: Fog blocks the view after 3 p.m.

name: Coffee-growing community
description: A visit to the cooperative of producer families: how the harvest is organized, fair trade and a home-cooked lunch prepared by the community.
tip: You can buy the cooperative's crafts and coffee directly here

name: Mercado Nacional de Artesanías
description: The old municipal market, restored as a stone fortress, brings together artisans from all over the country: hammocks, San Juan de Oriente ceramics and carved wood.
tip: Haggling is part of the custom, so do it with good humor

name: Parque Central and Catedral de San Jerónimo
description: Masaya's patron saint church, where the San Jerónimo festival takes place: one of the longest in Nicaragua, with processions and traditional dances.
tip: If your visit coincides with a procession, keep your distance and enjoy the music

name: Mirador del Volcán Masaya
description: One of the few volcanoes in the world where you can see an active lava lake from the crater rim, among sulfur fumaroles.
tip: At night you can sometimes see the glow of the lava; check the park's hours

name: Barrio Monimbó
description: Cradle of Nicaraguan folklore and of the 1978 insurrection: leather workshops, fireworks and the masks of the Torovenado dances.
tip: Ask about workshops open to the public to watch the artisans at work

name: Galería de Héroes y Mártires
description: A wall covered in portraits and murals that commemorates those who fell in the insurrection: the heart of Estelí's historical memory.
tip: Local guides often know personal stories about the families

name: Catedral de Estelí and Parque Central
description: Starting point of "the city of the boys": the central park, surrounded by shops and the daily life of Estelí.
tip: It's a good meeting point before or after the tour

name: Tour of an artisan cigar factory
description: Estelí makes some of the best cigars in the world. The tour shows the whole process, from selecting the leaf to hand rolling.
tip: You can buy directly from the factory at a better price than in stores

name: Mirador Tisey
description: Pine forest and a panoramic view over the Estelí valley, in a reserve known for its artisan cheeses and cool trails.
tip: Bring a light jacket: the area is cooler than the city center
